title: [observability] tmpfs_high reads a tmpfs alone: on a path whose filesystem is not a tmpfs (a /tmp on the root disk) nothing fires and an open one clears, naming the filesystem type (GitHub #66 part 2)
prompt:
Spawn, objective 215 [observability] (GitHub #66 part 2; owner t481u triage, lead-mac 16:15; author rev-h; readers rev-i, then rev-k): tmpfs_high reads a tmpfs alone.

Base: live main a599100c.

Where things stand. crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs read_tmpfs measures the used space of the filesystem holding SPAWN_ALERT_TMPFS_PATH (default /tmp) with df, fires over SPAWN_ALERT_TMPFS_HIGH_MB (8000) and clears under SPAWN_ALERT_TMPFS_OK_MB (6000). On a host whose /tmp is a directory of the root filesystem, "used" is the whole disk: the issue's alert read 61053 MiB on a 118 GB root, opened, and could never clear. Its name says a tmpfs; free disk already has its own alert (disk_low, objective 204).

What changes (spawn-cli alerts.rs, docs/fleet-architecture.md; no store or schema change):
(1) read_tmpfs first reads the statfs type of the path (rustix, already a dependency). On a tmpfs (TMPFS_MAGIC 0x01021994) nothing else changes: df's used MiB, the same thresholds, key, evidence and text.
(2) On a filesystem that is not a tmpfs there is no reading of a tmpfs: nothing fires, and an open tmpfs_high clears with evidence {path, not_tmpfs: true, fs_type: "0x<hex>", reading_ms}.
(3) A path statfs cannot read is a line in the loop's log, as df's failure is.
(4) No rename and no free-space variant: disk_low covers free disk.

Done when: rsi/scenarios/215.sh passes (fails with 1 on the base: the alert never clears on /usr); spawn-cli's unit test tmpfs_high_reads_a_tmpfs_alone_and_clears_on_a_path_that_is_not_one; check-clippy clean.
